children: Frankfurt’s DAX 40 rose about 0.7% to above 25,700 on Thursday, reaching its highest level in more than a week as oil prices continued to decline and global bond yields eased following the widely anticipated 25-basis-point rate hike by the US Federal Reserve.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh maintained a firm stance on inflation while avoiding a renewed surge in long-term yields, a combination that reassured investors.

Meanwhile, trade tensions were in focus after President Trump threatened the European Union with “very serious tariffs” or trade restrictions in response to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s proposal to pave the way for Canada to become the bloc’s first “associate member.” Most sectors traded in the green, led by industrials and autos.

title: DAX at Over 1-Week High
